text: Exactly one slicer per page, each one chosen specifically for what that particular page is actually meant to do — genuinely not five separate slicers sitting there that nobody will ever actually touch, which would recreate exactly the cluttered-dashboard problem Chapter Eight spent a whole lesson warning against.

Each individual page's slicer matches its own real purpose directly: year for comparing regional performance across time, category for narrowing profitability down to one product line at a time, and region for investigating whether fulfillment problems genuinely cluster in one specific area.

A hidden fourth page holds all the real underlying detail. Right-clicking any territory row on Page 1 jumps a viewer straight there, already pre-filtered to exactly that one territory, showing product-level breakdown underneath it — the summary page stays genuinely clean, while real detail sits just one click away for anyone who actually wants it.

Check every single page carefully before calling this done: selecting one bar should genuinely filter the rest of that same page automatically. If something doesn't respond the way you'd expect it to, that's Edit interactions at work — confirm it's truly intentional rather than simply an accident you overlooked along the way.

Interactivity added only exactly where it genuinely earns its place, and nowhere else at all beyond that — more interactivity isn't automatically better if a viewer ends up unsure what's even clickable. Lesson 91 finally publishes this entire finished project to the real Power BI service for the first time.
